title: The Trumpet and the Man Who Turned Away

paragraphs.text: The list of instructions given to the Prophet ends with one more command. He is told to be patient for the sake of his Lord, whatever difficulties he may face and whatever the people may say to him. Then the surah turns to the future. When the trumpet is blown, that Day will be extremely hard. For the disbelievers in particular, it will not be easy in any way at all, and there will be no relief for them on that Day. This short warning prepares the reader for the story that follows, which describes a man who heard the message clearly and still rejected it.

Allah tells the Prophet to leave to Him the man whom He created alone, with nothing. Allah then gave this man wide and plentiful wealth, and sons who stayed close beside him. He smoothed his life and made everything easy and comfortable for him. Yet even after all these blessings, the man still greedily wanted Allah to give him more. Allah answers firmly that this will not happen, because the man has been stubbornly hostile toward Allah's verses. Instead of more favors, he will be made to climb a hard and exhausting path of torment.

The surah describes the man's behavior very closely, step by step, almost as if the reader were watching him. When he heard the message, he thought carefully and planned what he would say about it. Allah condemns him for the way he planned, and then condemns him once again, because his plan was meant to oppose the truth. He looked around once more and considered the matter again. Then his face changed: he frowned and scowled with displeasure. Finally, he turned his back on the message and behaved with arrogance, refusing to accept what he had heard. His careful thinking did not lead him to faith; it only led him to pride. His story shows how a person can receive many gifts from Allah, hear His verses with full understanding, and still choose to turn away from them.
